title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous pages. K is a field of finite type over Q. Γ_K = Gal(K̄/K). Π_K is the geometric part (the kernel of Γ_K → Γ_Q). Σ_K is the corresponding extension of (an open subgroup of) Γ_Q by Π_K. The conjecture under discussion is a Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture: suitable outer homomorphisms Σ_{K'} → Σ_K compatible with the projections to Γ_Q should come from Q-embeddings K → K' (up to Frobenius-free twisting). The previous page had already found that the naive statement needs correction, using centralizers of the open subgroups Σ'^o (kernel of the cyclotomic character).

This page makes three moves.
(1) The Γ_K are 'too big' to work with directly. One should view Γ_K as the projective limit lim_U π_1(U) = lim Γ_{U/Q}, where U runs over affine (smooth) models of K over Q. This holds because K̄ is the union of the finite étale covers of the models after shrinking.
(2) One should focus on models that are 'elementary varieties' in Artin's sense: successive smooth fibrations in affine curves with good compactification. These are profinite K(π,1)'s in characteristic 0 (SGA 4 XI). More generally one can use any model that is a profinite K(π,1), so that the étale homotopy type of U is the classifying topos of Γ_{U/Q}.
(3) Proposed refinement of the Hom-conjecture. Beyond the anabelian hypothesis and compatibility with the maps to Γ_Q, one should perhaps require the homomorphism Σ_{K'} → Σ_K to be compatible with the 'filtrations' on these groups induced by the models. These are the coarse 'modular filtrations': the inverse system of kernels Ker(Γ_K → Γ_{U/Q}), generated by inertia at divisors removed from the models. Compatibility means that for each model U of K there is a model V of K' such that the map descends to Γ_{V/Q} → Γ_{U/Q}. That is a necessary condition for geometric origin, since a dominant map of function fields extends to models after shrinking.

The last line, continued on the next page, sets the programme: study in parallel the fields of finite type, the homomorphisms between them and their Galois groups, and the analogous situation for elementary anabelian (or general K(π,1)) models U, V and maps of Galois topoi B_V → B_U over B_Q.
errors: No outright error. The limit statement Γ_K = lim π_1(U) needs U to run over normal (smooth) models, and if K is not regular over Q one must work over the algebraic closure of Q in K. Grothendieck glosses over this.
Elementary varieties being profinite K(π,1)'s is correct in characteristic 0 (Artin, SGA 4 Exp. XI). It is asserted without comment.

The proposed extra hypothesis (compatibility with the model filtrations) is put forward only as 'il est possible qu'il faille'. Its precise formulation is not given: which filtration, and with what indexing.

ideas.what: Absolute Galois group of a finitely generated field as projective limit of étale fundamental groups of its affine models
ideas.modern_name: Γ_K = lim π_1^et(U) over models (birational anabelian set-up)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA 1); used systematically by Pop, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 (generic point of a normal scheme); implicitly in Esquisse d'un programme / letter to Faltings 1983

ideas.what: Restrict attention to elementary (Artin) varieties, or more generally profinite K(π,1) models
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin (SGA 4 XI); 'elementary anabelian' terminology Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Strengthen the Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture by requiring compatibility with the 'modular filtrations' (system of kernels Γ_K → π_1(U) over models)
ideas.modern_name: Respecting inertia / decomposition structure of divisors; 'filtration-preserving' or 'geometric-type' conditions in Hom-form anabelian theorems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related conditions appear in Pop (birational anabelian, 1990s, local theory of divisorial inertia), Mochizuki (Hom-form for curves over sub-p-adic fields, 1999), and later 'inertia-preserving' conditions
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or letter to Faltings to my knowledge

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests that the Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture over Q (for fields of finite type of any dimension) should probably include an extra hypothesis: compatibility with the coarse 'modular filtrations' of Γ_K given by the system of models. This turns the field version into a pro-system of model versions. The idea is not developed further here.
missed.quote: qu'elles soient compatibles avec les filtrations sur ces groupes, associées à ces modèles ("filtrations modulaires" (grossières))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The Hom-form for higher-dimensional function fields over number fields remains open; the isomorphism form is Pop's theorem. A filtration/inertia-compatibility hypothesis of this type is close to what is known to be needed in practice. It documents Grothendieck's own awareness that the naive Hom-conjecture needs correction. That is of historical interest but not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck self-correcting the field-theoretic Hom-conjecture and proposing an inertia/model-filtration compatibility condition. That is a mildly interesting unpublished nuance, but it is close in spirit to conditions specialists later imposed (Pop, Mochizuki). The rest (limit over models, elementary K(π,1) varieties) is standard or published in the Esquisse and the Faltings letter.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{E}_{K'} \to \mathcal{E}_K$' is very likely '$\Sigma_{K'} \to \Sigma_K$' (same notation as the previous page), with 'ext' written above as in 'homs ext' (outer homomorphisms).

'dégagée[?], préciser[?] en demandant[?] en plus de' should probably read roughly 'dans ces hyp. d'avoir (en plus de l'hyp. anabélienne et de la compatibilité avec les homs des Γ_Q)'. The parenthesis opens before 'en plus'.
'qu'elles soient' agrees with an implicit plural (the homomorphisms). The struck word before 'des K(π,1)' is a deleted 'sont'.
